newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Brent, gas oil rally to continue short term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Brent, gas oil rally to continue short term.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20

----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - July 31------------- * Look for the rally to continue in the short term but when it does fail it will probably come down and test the lows and break them. * Brent has completed a 50 percent retracement of the $20.40 high of May 16 from the low of $17.70 on June 20, but a similar rally failed when the market hesitated around $19 on July 2.

IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures gapped bullishly higher on Wednesday and with good support in place, little in the way of resistance and technical indicators leaving room for more gains, the trend looks set to continue, analysts said.
Nicholas Wilson analyst at MeesPierson Isle of Man said: "Look for the rally to continue in the short term but when it does fail it will probably come down and test the lows and probably break them".
Only very short-term indicators for gas oil are flagging signs of a possible correction with the five-day RSI at 83 percent the only real bearish signal in the London markets at the moment.

Market leader on both sides of the Atlantic, NYMEX gasoline, continues to look increasingly overbought short term with the five-day RSI at 94 percent and nine-day RSI at 87 percent indicating room for a short term correction.

However, some analysts say that the market is showing increased volatility because of a possible squeeze on the August gasoline contract which expires at the close of business today and much will depend on what happens to the Aug/Sep spread today, currently around 7.5 cents in backwardation, as to how any correction unfolds.
Even here though good support is in place on the September gasoline chart with longer term indicators remaining neutral.
On the spot month continuation chart for Brent only good support levels can be picked out with the market having few technically bearish signs.
Even the recent expanding wedge pattern, usually a bearish signal, is starting to unwind following a series of consecutive higher highs and higher lows over past eight days.

The next challenge is for the Brent market is to get convincingly above $19, after this there is little in it's way until $20.60. The $19 level was printed near the close on Wednesday but dipped back to close a $18.97.
On the September chart prices ended well above trendline support that has been tested but not breached over the past seven trading days. This support comes in at around $18.90 today.
The contract also gapped above downtrend resistance stemming from May 16's and May 20's double-top of $20.40 that capped it's progress on Monday and Tuesday at $18.70.

"The market has completed a 50 percent retracement of the $20.40 high of May 16 from the low of $17.70 on June 20, but a similar rally failed when the market hesitated around $19 on July 2," Wilson said.
However, he looks for the rally to continue to $19.37 which represents a .618 Fibonacci retracement of the $20.40-$17.70 range with the May 29 and the June 2 $19.80 the ultimate target.
The bearish effects of a "contracting triangle" on the September chart moving upward from consolidation on June 20 that ended at $18.70 were eliminated when the market printed $18.97 at the close.
Analysts said the picture for gas oil looks similarly rosy.
On the spot month chart prices gapped higher leaving good support in place between $166.75 Tuesday's low and Wednesday's $169 open.

"Look for the rally to extend to $175 a significant level represented by the $175.75-$174.75 gap down from the June 3 to June 4 and there is also a .618 Fibonacci retracement at a shade over $165," Wilson said.
However, short term RSIs with the five-day marker at 83 percent are flagging a correction which analysts say could come as a result of any fall-out stemming from the NYMEX products expiry.
On the September chart slow stochastics are on the point of crossing at a high level signalling a correction but the market is well supported up from July 15's $160 trough.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
